newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares firmer at outset of bourse dealings.
newsitem.headline: German shares firmer at outset of bourse dealings.

text.p: Germany's 30-share DAX index was firmer in early quiet bourse dealings on Monday as the market got a boost from the dollar rising about one pfennig from last Friday and ongoing Wall Street gains.

The DAX index was up 4.57 points at 3,799.98 points but off the session high so far at 3,808.09 points. The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings, was down 11.72 points at 3,798.20 points.
Dealers said the positive effect of gains in other markets and the moderate rise in the U.S. dollar had helped market sentiment in Germany.
A further gain in the dollar to above 1.74 marks further buoyed the market before the DAX pared some gains on a modest bout of profit-taking, they said.
The outlook for the German share market would depend in part on the extent to which major fund houses had already finished squaring off their positions for the first half.
Further major market impulses were not expected this week.
The U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-making committee meeting would of course be watched, but with no interest rate move expected little market impact was seen likely.
Chemical and automotive stocks were expected to be the focus of trading during the day.
Luxury carmaker Porsche AG was a top percentage gainer, rising 115 marks to 2,245 marks due to the stronger dollar, while chemical group Bayer AG was up one mark at 68 marks.
